analysis: Overnight trade reads as AI-rally fatigue meeting macro pushback. Tuesday's record close (S&P 500 and Nasdaq at all-time highs) was carried by megacaps, and that concentration is now the story itself: Bespoke says six of the 13 trillion-dollar stocks look overbought, UBS's Haefele warns on narrowing breadth, and Dalio called AI a 'classic bubble' approaching (not yet at) its bursting point. Against that, the 30-year yield hit its highest since 2002 (5.70%) ahead of today's Fed minutes, and Brent retook $100 on Hormuz/Houthi headlines — the two forces that can interrupt an AI-led tape. Two reversals overnight: Monday's Terafab scare (Musk confirming TSMC talks) partially unwound — Intel +1.3% after Bloomberg said it stays on the project, TSMC -1.5%. And SpaceX's -2.1% on the FT's $40B chip-financing scoop is single-source headline risk, not a confirmed demand event — NVDA barely moving (-0.2%) is the tell. Nothing here contradicts yesterday's setup: futures are only slightly lower and the Mag7 was still firm in premarket (WSJ). Community signal was thin: HN carried the FT SpaceX/Nvidia story with zero comments, and no qualifying Reddit threads surfaced. USAC has no fresh news; its TXSE debut and Zacks' upward estimate revisions remain the standing context.
disclaimer: Not financial advice — for informational purposes only.

headlines.headline: Fed September-meeting minutes release today (2pm ET / 1800 GMT). October-hike odds have fallen to 22% (LSEG) from ~70% at the start of last week after soft August PCE and a weak September payrolls print (29,000 vs 90,000 estimate), but the September meeting itself raised rates to 3.75-4.00% with 16 of 18 officials projecting at least one more hike this year.
headlines.why_it_matters: Sets the rates-path tone into the open — the market wants to know whether the minutes read as a peak or as a pause before another move.

headlines.headline: Futures slip premarket: Dow E-minis -178 (-0.34%), S&P 500 E-minis -11.25 (-0.14%), Nasdaq 100 E-minis -129.25 (-0.41%). The 30-year Treasury yield rose to 5.70%, its highest since 2002; Brent retook $100 ($101.20, +0.6%) and WTI neared $90 after Iran intensified tanker attacks in the Strait of Hormuz and Houthi militants hit Saudi airports.
headlines.why_it_matters: Risk-off premarket flavor — a resumed bond selloff plus rebounding oil prices work against yesterday's record tape.

headlines.headline: The Magnificent Seven kept strengthening in premarket trade even as Dow futures lagged; Tuesday's session closed with the S&P 500 and Nasdaq at all-time highs while the Dow remains ~5% below its August 5 record close.
headlines.why_it_matters: Concentration trade persists — megacap AI names are still the tape's engine, but UBS flags the narrowing breadth as the risk-management cue.

headlines.headline: SpaceX (SPCX) fell 2.1-2.2% premarket after the Financial Times reported the company is seeking $40 billion in financing (Apollo-led) to fund purchases of Nvidia chips; Nvidia slipped 0.2%.
headlines.why_it_matters: Financing overhang on the newest trillion-dollar name — but single-source, unconfirmed: no SpaceX or Nvidia confirmation, so treat as fragile; NVDA barely moving is the tell that no confirmed demand event exists yet.

headlines.headline: Intel rose 1.3% after a Bloomberg report that it will continue working on Elon Musk's Terafab chipmaking venture; TSMC dropped 1.5% after Musk downplayed its role.
headlines.why_it_matters: Partial reversal of Monday's 4% Intel slide after Musk confirmed TSMC talks — de-risks the foundry-partner narrative; the real debate (whether Intel can deliver 14A at volume) is still open.

headlines.headline: Constellation Brands (STZ) dropped 4.9% premarket after beating Q2 earnings targets but signaling weak underlying demand for Modelo Especial and Corona Extra.
headlines.why_it_matters: Classic beat-but-soft-guide pattern — revenue quality, not the headline beat, sets the open.

headlines.headline: FICO slipped 0.1% after announcing it will cut 15% of staff and integrate AI-driven product development.
headlines.why_it_matters: Another AI-driven restructuring datapoint for software/services margins — small premarket move, more narrative than tape.
